**Why:** both are the cleanest downtrends in the pool and both are in profit. I2609 is the weakest contract overall (762→699, -8%) with OI falling as price falls. I scaled in on today's weak bounce rather than at the lows, which keeps my average above market.

**Risk state:** risk ratio 55.5% (was 35.0%), available 44,172, margin call line at 80% and force-close at 100% — I have roughly 24,500 of room before margin call, so this is a controlled size increase, not a stretch.

**What I deliberately did not do:** CU2610 was the single best-looking chart (new high 106790, OI 116k→129k) but one lot needs 53,250 margin and would have pushed risk ratio to ~89%, straight through the margin-call line — I passed on the best chart because it didn't fit the account, not because it wasn't a good trade. IM2609 I also skipped: it closed at the top of a month-long 6650–7270 chop range, and at 216k/lot margin it was unaffordable anyway.

**One note for the log:** the initial RB order returned a Windows file-lock error (`account.json` temp-file rename failure), not a rule rejection. I retried once after confirming it was an I/O fault and it filled. Worth flagging if it recurs — it's an infrastructure issue that could silently drop orders.

**Open risk to watch:** RB and I are both black-complex shorts, so this is essentially one directional bet across two correlated legs. If iron ore rallies back through the 712–725 shelf that rejected in late July, both legs bleed together — that's my cue to cut the I leg first, since it carries the larger per-point loss (100 multiplier).
